Jamal: Hey @Ana (People Ops) — quick question. We onboarded ~12 folks from the acquired team on Nov 18. They have unused PTO on their old plan that didn't transfer. A few have more than our 5-day carryover cap. Is there any process to grant a one-time exception or extended window to use those days? Some can't take time off before the year-end shutdown.

Ana (People Ops): Welcome Jamal — thanks for flagging. Short answer: we can approve limited exceptions in acquisition cases, but they need manager and People Ops sign-off and must be submitted before the payroll cutoff. Our standard carryover policy: up to 5 days roll into the next year. Exceptions are evaluated case-by-case (duration of transition, inability to use days due to policies at previous employer). Please have managers submit the exception request form with dates and rationale. Example request body we need:

```
Employee: Name (email)
Date joined Redwood: 2025-11-18
Untransferred PTO days: 8
Requested carryover days: 5 (extra 3 exception)
Rationale: Onboarding & org transition prevented use; prior employer policy blocked payout.
Manager endorsement: <manager notes>
```

Form: https://hr.redwood.internal/pto-exceptions (internal)
Payroll cutoff for submitting exceptions this cycle is Dec 15 EOD PST. If you miss it we can consider emergency approvals but they may not be processed until the next payroll cycle.

Marta (Manager): Thanks Ana — I'll submit for Lina, Omar, and Priya today. Lina has 7 days, Omar 6, Priya 9. I can endorse the extra days for Lina and Priya; Omar's is borderline but I'll include context about travel restrictions during onboarding.

Jamal: Also — the year-end shutdown week (Dec 27–31) is a mandatory off-week. If someone wants to use carried-over days to cover additional days around that shutdown (like taking Dec 22–26), is that allowed before approvals come through? And what's typical approval turnaround?

Ana (People Ops): Year-end shutdown is company-wide and unpaid if you don't have balance. Carried-over days can be used to make days paid around the shutdown, but approvals must be in place before the manager marks time-off in the system. Turnaround: we aim for 3 business days for straightforward cases. If a manager submits with enough context and the employee has documented inability to use prior PTO, we usually approve within 48–72 hours. If it's time-sensitive (travel/family plans) please cc payroll@redwood.team to expedite.

PayrollBot: Note: payroll cutoff for this catalog year exceptions = 2025-12-15T23:59:00 PST. Submissions after this date may roll to Q1 processing.

Marta (Manager): Got it — filing the three requests now and cc'ing payroll. Thanks! :+1:

Jamal: Perfect, thanks Ana and Marta. I'll follow up if any of the folks need documentation from their old employer.
